question.problem: Which root(s) of the polynomial $p(x)=7{x}^{3}+42{x}^{2}$ have multiplicity $2?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to factor the polynomial. 

For this polynomial, we can factor by noting that the greatest common factor of $7{x}^{3}$ and $42{x}^{2}$ is $7{x}^{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}p(x) & =7{x}^{3}+42{x}^{2} \\  & =7{x}^{2}(x+6)\end{aligned}
$$

To find the roots and their multiplicities, we look at the factors:

- The factor $x$ has an exponent of $2$ in the factored form of $p(x).$ So the root $x=0$ has multiplicity $2.$

- The factor $(x+6)$ has an exponent of $1$ in the factored form of $p(x).$ So the root $x=-6$ has multiplicity $1.$

In conclusion, only the root $x=0$ has multiplicity $2.$
